scope: four hand-authored sanity cases; not a benchmark of research quality

expected.algorithm: At t, output interval C_t from H_(t-1). Then observe y_t, update H_t, and choose alpha_next for the interval at t+1.
At t, observe y_t, append residual |y_t - prediction_t| to H, calibrate q from H, and report [prediction_t-q, prediction_t+q] for the same t as an out-of-sample interval.

alpha is miscoverage; interval radius is Q(1-alpha) for the same fixed residual list. When no candidate is feasible, use the smallest alpha in the grid to obtain the widest candidate interval. No coverage guarantee is claimed.
alpha is miscoverage; interval radius is Q(1-alpha) for the same fixed residual list. Use the largest alpha in the grid and claim this gives the widest candidate interval.

answers.reason: Input H_(t-1) precedes y_t; update uses y_t for future alpha_next at t+1, no leakage.
Residual uses y_t before interval calculation at same t, causing label leakage.
Smallest alpha implies largest (1-alpha), yielding widest quantile interval logically.
Largest alpha implies smallest (1-alpha), yielding narrowest quantile interval, contradicting claim.
C_t uses H_(t-1); y_t enters H_t only after C_t.
y_t is used in H before reporting the interval at the same t.
Smallest alpha gives largest 1-alpha and widest Q(1-alpha).
Largest alpha gives smallest 1-alpha and narrower Q(1-alpha).
